The four-head removal beats head 3 alone problem by problem as well: on DEV[1024:1250], 28 problems are solved only by T1-all against 15 only by T1 (85 by both). The equivalence check failed only because of a shape mistake (one shared 256-wide value head feeds four 256-column output blocks); I redo it per head below.

The model-wide comparison singles out L11's value pathway on all three measures:

| Measure | L11 | Next highest |
|---|---|---|
| End-of-prompt value math-specificity, vs poem value | 2.8 | 2.0 (L13, L20) |
| Same, vs mean answer value | 7.3 | 4.5 (L23), 4.4 (L10) |
| v_proj gain on the math residual direction, vs its average gain | 1.55 | 1.13 (L10); all others 0.20–0.85 |

So L11's v_proj is the one value projection in the model tuned to the math-task direction of the residual stream. It produces an outsized math-task value at the end-of-prompt token, which all L11 heads, head 3 most of all, carry into every answer token. This is both weight and activation evidence for the location of the brake, and it matches the causal ordering: T1 +25.7 < T1-all +31.4.

I therefore express the edit where the anomaly sits: one rank-1 projection on L11's v_proj output, v_proj → (I − v̂v̂ᵀ)·v_proj, with o_proj restored to the original. It is mathematically identical to T1-all; I verify that per head. I measure this exact tensor from now on, first on DEV[0:256] (T1 +19.9, T1r2 +17.6 there) and then on HOLDOUT.

The v_proj form matches the four-head o_proj form to within bf16 rounding: the largest entry-wise difference is 2–4×10⁻⁴, against typical entries of 8×10⁻³. Only L11's v_proj is edited now. The math-task component of its output drops from 1.474 to 0.002, which is a rank-1 change carrying 0.7% of the tensor's energy (8.3% relative Frobenius change).

I run it paired on DEV[0:256], where T1 gave +19.9 and T1r2 +17.6.
- If V1 again beats head-3-only removal, I freeze V1 as the candidate and move to HOLDOUT.
- If it falls clearly below T1, the +5.7 advantage on the other slice was noise, and I would freeze the narrower T1.

V1 holds and repeats its advantage. On DEV[0:256] it gives +25.4 ± 3.3 points (76 wrong→right, 11 right→wrong), lifting accuracy from 22.3% to 47.7%, against 42.2% for head-3-only removal (T1) and 39.8% for T1r2 on the same problems. Over both DEV slices (482 problems), V1 averages about +28 points, consistently 5–6 points above T1. Removing the math-task signal from L11's shared value stream is the better repair.

The remaining question before freezing is whether the plant has a matching key or query side. Head 2 attends to the end-of-prompt token much more on math (0.27 against 0.07 for the poem). If L11's key projection is also tuned to the math direction, the end-of-prompt token would still draw extra attention on math problems after V1. It would now carry a neutral value, but would still dilute the heads' attention to useful tokens.

I check this from weights and summary vectors only:
- the gain of each layer's k_proj (and, for L11, of each head's q_proj) on that layer's math residual direction, relative to its average gain, with the same measure that flagged L11's v_proj at 1.55;
- at L11, the attention score that the mean answer-token query of each head gives to the math versus the poem end-of-prompt key.

An L11 k_proj outlier, or a large math-minus-poem score gap for head 2 or 3, would make a key-side edit the next candidate. If nothing stands out, I freeze V1 and go to HOLDOUT.

Nothing on the key or query side points to a second plant. L11's k_proj gain on the math direction is ordinary: 0.68, within the model's range of 0.22–1.03. The L11 query gains are 0.74–1.16, also ordinary.

Head 2 does score the math end-of-prompt key higher than the poem one: +60 unscaled, about +3.7 logits after the 1/16 scaling, against +1 to +1.6 for the other heads. But that comes from ordinary weights, and the estimate ignores RoPE, so it is only indicative. With V1 that token now carries no math-task value, so attending to it is close to harmless.

The anomaly is specific to the value path. L11's v_proj is the only value projection that amplifies the math-task direction (1.55× its average gain). Removing that one output direction gives the largest and most consistent gains: +31.4 and +25.4 on two DEV slices, against +25.7 and +19.9 for head-3-only removal.

I now freeze V1 as the candidate and confirm it on HOLDOUT, which has not been used for any choice. HOLDOUT's 1,000 problems go into four disjoint slices of 250, one paired pass each, pooled at the end. A pooled gain well above zero, around +20 or more with a standard error near 1.6, confirms the edit. A much smaller gain would mean the DEV estimates were inflated by selection.
